sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Sensitive key name list
sections.what: Defines the key names that count as sensitive, such as token, password, secret, authorization, cookie and several provider key headers.
sections.why: The header states it covers standard secret names plus provider headers and app-specific names.
sections.watch_out: A new secret name, such as a new provider header, must be added here or it will be logged.

sections.name: redactSensitive
sections.title: Copying and cleaning nested data
sections.what: Walks through a value, replaces sensitive-named fields with a placeholder, and returns a new copy.
sections.why: The header states the input is never changed and that loops are handled.
sections.watch_out: Secrets written inside plain text strings are not caught by this function.

summary: Returns a copy of any object with values under sensitive key names replaced by a placeholder.
purpose: Keep passwords, tokens and keys out of logs.
why: The header states the redaction exists before response bodies and headers are written to logs.
how: Walks through objects and lists. Any key whose whole name matches the sensitive list gets its value replaced. It tracks the objects above the current one to stop endless loops.
inputs: Any value, plus an internal tracking set that callers normally leave alone.
outputs: A new cleaned copy. The original is not changed.
risks: Only whole key names are matched. A secret under another name, or inside a plain text string, is not hidden.
debug: If a secret still appears in a log, check its key name against the sensitive list. If the output shows Circular, the input contains a loop.
